explanation: Laurel was sacred to Apollo, and Latin laureatus, 'crowned with laurel', gives English 'laureate'. Olympic victors in ancient Greece received wreaths of wild olive instead.

claims.text: A Roman general celebrating a triumph wore a laurel wreath.
The triumphal wreath was not made of olive, ivy or oak leaves.
The laurel was sacred to Apollo.
English 'laureate' comes from Latin laureatus, 'crowned with laurel'.
Victors at the ancient Olympic Games received wreaths of wild olive.
